DEEPAK GUPTA, J.
Prayer in this pe on led under Sec on 482 of the Bhar ya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (old Sec on 438 Cr.P.C.) is for grant of an cipatory bail in case FIR No.59 dated 17.06.2024, registered at Police Sta on Cyber Crime, Sector 17, UT, Chandigarh, under Sec ons 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B IPC.

sentences.text: 2. FIR was lodged on the complaint of one Krishan Lal Gupta, as per which on 26.05.2024, he received a phone call from mobile No.94172-49922.

The caller disclosed his name as Naveen and told him that a parcel had been booked on his Aadhar Card, which was being sent to Mohammed Naseem and that the same has been held by the Custom Department, as it was containing banned item.
As the complainant told that he had not sent any such parcel, he was asked to make a complaint to the Cyber Police Sta on.

Complainant was connected online to a person named Parkash, who made inquiries from the complainant and photo of his Aadhar Card was called for,
which was sent by him.

Therea=er, complainant received a call that his Aadhar Card had been used at several places and on the basis thereof, 04 accounts had been opened, which were used for money laundering and that 8.4 million Page no.1 out of 4 pages 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132973 CRM-M-49806-2024 dollars had been sent abroad and that he (complainant) could be arrested.
Complainant was further told that he had been digitally arrested.

He was then connected to one DCP Dr. Baljit Singh Rajput, who asked him to deposit  45,08,500/-
in SBI account No.42639801550.
Complainant transferred the said amount from his bank account by a cheque.
It was alleged by the complainant that he had been cheated and so, necessary ac on be taken.

sentences.text: Necessary inquiry was conducted and then the present FIR was registered.

During inves ga on,
the details of bank account No.42639801550 were collected and it was found to be in the name of Parmar Collec ons, Kamal Ali, Shop No.2, Raigarh, Maharastra.

It was found that an amount of 45,08,500/- was transacted from the said account to dierent bank accounts including the account of Gopal Soni (pe oner) and that in his account, an amount of  4,40,000/- was received and the same was withdrawn vide cheque No.097483 for  3,00,000/- and cheque No.097484 for 1,40,000/- on 28.05.2024.
Raids were conducted to apprehend the pe oner, but he escaped.
No ce under Sec on 41-A Cr.P.C. was also served on 30.06.2024 to his brother direc ng him to produce the pe oner, but he failed to appear.

4. It is contended by learned counsel for the pe oner that the pe oner has been falsely implicated;
that in fact he is vic m of his benevolent nature of helping somebody in need.
It is contended that a boy named Shiv Partap used to study with the pe oner in library, where pe oner used to go for prepara on of his compe ve examina on.
Said boy Shiv Partap told the pe oner that his father is abroad and he (Shiv Pratap) is in emergent need of money for the treatment of his ailing mother.

Said Shiv Partap further told the complainant that as he did not have the cheque book of his account, Page no.2 out of 4 pages 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132973 CRM-M-49806-2024 therefore, he requested the pe oner to help him by allowing him to get transfer of an amount of  4-5 lacs in his account from his father, so that he can withdraw the said amount through the pe oner's cheque book.

Learned counsel contends that believing the said story put forth by Shiv Partap as genuine, pe oner gave his consent and this way, Shiv Partap got transferred the amount in the pe oner's account and later on, the whole amount was withdrawn through two cheques.
5. Learned counsel further contends that when pe oner approached the bank to withdraw the some loan amount, he came to know that his bank account has been freezed.
He then approached Shiv Partap, but no sa sfactory reply was given to him.

He became suspicious that said Shiv Partap alongwith his accomplice Rajpal was involved in some fraudulent ac vi es and then he (pe oner)
made a complaint dated 17.06.2024 against them.
Learned counsel contends that pe oner is s ll ready to join the inves ga on and so, in all these circumstances, he be allowed an cipatory bail.

6. On advance no ce, Mr. Manish Kumar Bansal, PP for U.T., Chandigarh has appeared and strongly opposed the bail pe on by poin ng out that amount of  4,40,000/- out of the defrauded amount of 45,08,500/- by way of Cyber crime was received in the bank account of the pe oner and that said amount of  4,40,000/- was withdrawn by way of two cheques on 28.05.2024.

Despite the fact that the FIR was lodged on 17.06.2024, no complaint or representa on was ever made by the pe oner prior to 03.08.2024, as is evident from the index indica ng that he had made representa on Annexures P-3 and P-4 to the C.M., Rajasthan and IG (Police), Ajmer.

Learned state counsel contends further that looking into the nature of allega ons and aFribu on to the pe oner, inasmuch as a part of the defrauded amount has been Page no.3 out of 4 pages 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:132973 CRM-M-49806-2024 received in his account, his custodial interroga on is required and so, his bail pe on be declined.
7.
I have considered submissions of both the sides and have appraised the record carefully.

sentences.text: Apparently, it is a case of Cyber crime.
Amount of  45,08,500/- was transferred by the complainant in an account number given to him under the threat to be arrested, as his account was allegedly used for the purpose of money laundering.

It has been found that various transac ons took place from that account, in which the amount of  45,08,500/- was transferred and that an amount of  4,40,000/- was transferred in the account of the pe oner, which was later on withdrawn by way of two cheques on 28.05.2024.

The story put forth by the pe oner that he used to meet a boy, namely Shiv Parkash in the library and on his asking, he consented for his account to be used, appears to be imsy and concocted at this stage.
Considering the nature of allega ons and the gravity of the oence, custodial interroga on of the pe oner may be necessary to unearth the en re truth.
9. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court is not inclined to grant the benet of an cipatory bail to the pe oner.
As such, without commen ng on the merits of the case, the present pe on is hereby dismissed.
October 07, 2024 (DEEPAK GUPTA)
